title: ModuLair: Streamlining Python Virtual Environment Management for HPC
problem: Managing Python environments on HPC systems is complex due to toolchains, file system constraints, and diverse user needs; existing solutions lack integrated CLI/GUI support.
motivation: Python users on HPC systems struggle with environment setup and reproducibility; reducing this barrier enables broader adoption of computational science.
method: ModuLair automates Python virtual environment setup (containers that isolate different Python package versions) using metadata (configuration files) on HPC systems. It works with both EasyBuild (software used to automate software installation on HPC systems) and other module systems. It provides command-line and graphical interfaces—including Jupyter, Drona Composer, and the HPRC Dashboard—so users can manage environments however they prefer.
key_novelty: ModuLair is the first virtual environment framework that automatically detects an HPC's module system and manages Python environments through configuration files, accessible via both command-line and graphical interfaces.
contributions: Automatic detection of EasyBuild vs non-EasyBuild systems
Integrated CLI interface for power users
Integrated GUI via HPRC Dashboard and Drona Composer
limitations: Abstract-only; lacks quantitative metrics on adoption rates, setup time reduction, or error reduction compared to baseline approaches
